scope: Source proxy/runtime termination and actual local Linux named-volume isolation. Docker Desktop Linux/arm64, not the personal HTTPS VM or an installed native application.

reproduced_before_fix.cause: Linux PID 1 had no SIGTERM handler. Docker stop waited five seconds then used SIGKILL. The first mount-only probe did not distinguish this from clean termination.

implementation: Shared stdlib-only proxy termination context registers SIGTERM on the asyncio loop, requests cooperative stop and restores the previous signal policy.
The standalone proxy owns that context across initialization, listener lifetime and ledger close. A startup stop returns before replacing the listener.
Added a thin Linux framework consumer, explicit non-default Docker acceptance and a source-only test image recipe; existing daemon/project binding and cleanup-only grants are reused unchanged.
verified: Proxy and controller actually run as uid/gid 1001 in separate Linux containers. Only the trusted proxy mounts the private ledger and real Docker socket.
The controller has a writable root. Its fake ownership file at the same absolute path stays in its own filesystem and does not corrupt or replace proxy authority.
The controller cannot see the original private ledger or real socket, and its attempt to mount the known private volume through the filtered Docker API is rejected.
Both ordinary stop/start and SIGKILL/start retain committed cleanup-only receipts. The old stopped worker never starts and explicit recovery removes it.
Ordinary stop exits 0 with cooperative listener/ledger close; explicit SIGKILL exits 137. Neither result is inferred merely from eventual container removal.
Native Linux persistence/policy checks cover modes, unsafe paths, daemon/project changes, corrupt receipts, writer locking, wire bounds, failed writes and signal restoration.
The 231 affected regressions and all nine host-side actual proxy cases pass after the fix, preserving legacy memory-only and no-adoption behavior.
Every temporary controller/proxy container and named volume is removed. The unrelated llm-cli-proxy service remains running.

fixture.build_inputs: Current framework source, proxy/helper files, two unit-test modules and the thin consumer. The repository-pinned official Docker CLI was downloaded during explicit fixture preparation.
fixture.runtime: Network none, no capabilities, no-new-privileges and bounded resources. Proxy root is read-only; controller root is writable. Shared socket and Studio data are separate from private proxy storage.
fixture.real_daemon_socket: Mounted read-only only in the trusted proxy, whose Docker authority is root-equivalent as in the existing deployment. It is never mounted into the controller.

migration.upgrade: Update the standalone launcher and matching framework policy, then restart the selected deployment. Private state/helper configuration remains as documented.
migration.rollback: Stop proxy-backed work before reverting; the old PID 1 behavior can require Docker forced termination. Existing receipts remain compatible.

pending: Personal HTTPS VM deployment: real host bind paths, mapped UID/GID, Docker socket group, TLS/auth, upgrades and full restore.
Actual host power-loss, Docker daemon restart and remote/SSH disruption. Named-volume and process-kill proof does not certify those events.
Physical devices, selected provider accounts, escaped MCP descendants and native/frozen/installed OS acceptance remain separate.
Uncommitted/evicted/unrecorded ownership still requires review; no name-based adoption was added. Host administrators and the proxy remain trusted.

quality.ruff: Changed runtime/consumer/tests pass with the already documented legacy N818 exception-name rule excluded.

release_note: A disposable acceptance image was built; no desktop app or installer was rebuilt. Existing manifest is unchanged; absent DMGs were not recreated or reverified.
